name: llama-cpp-kleidiai-cuda-ngl0-devnone
description: Reproduction rig for ggml-org/llama.cpp#26334: llama-cli built with -DGGML_CPU_KLEIDIAI=ON -DGGML_CUDA=ON, run with -ngl 0 (CPU-only inference) and WITH -dev none (the maintainer-documented workaround). Not an upstream-shipped preset -- a one-off variant of tools/targets/llama-cpp-kleidiai.json with -ngl 0 appended to the workload, created only to drive this reproduction. Committed 2026-08-06 with the verified_against receipt for the 2026-08-05 measurement session -- the same run whose captured output still shows the 'marked untested' warning, reflecting this preset's receipt-less state at run time (see caveats and results/upstream/NOTE-TARGET-VALIDATION-WARNING.md).
why_it_matters: Per make_cpu_buft_list() in src/llama-model.cpp, when a CUDA device is present in the model's devices list (independent of -ngl, which only zeroes compute-offloaded layers) and --no-host/-dev none are NOT passed, a GPU host (pinned-memory) buffer type is inserted into the CPU buffer-type priority list ahead of KleidiAI's extra-buft entry. select_weight_buft() then picks the first accepting buft in list order, so tensors are given the CUDA host buft before KleidiAI's extra buft is ever tried -- silently bypassing KleidiAI even though -ngl 0 was passed and the KLEIDIAI=1 banner still prints. This is the exact mechanism ggml-org/llama.cpp#26334's reporter (izard) described and gaugarg-nv (NVIDIA CUDA-backend maintainer) confirmed with a doc/policy-level reply; the issue was closed via a documented workaround, not a code fix, and nobody in the thread produced a measured before/after.

l1.note: Unchanged from tools/targets/llama-cpp-kleidiai.json -- same regex, same family order.

patterns.label: buffer_type_fallback
patterns.regex: cannot be used with preferred buffer type (\S+)

patterns.label: no_kernel_warning
patterns.regex: kleidiai: no kernel for tensor type (\S+), not accelerated

l2.note: Unchanged from tools/targets/llama-cpp-kleidiai.json. 'buffer_type_fallback' is the one existing pattern most relevant to #26334: with --verbose (see workload) llama.cpp's verbosity threshold is raised to INT_MAX, which includes LLAMA_LOG_DEBUG -- so the 'cannot be used with preferred buffer type X, using Y instead' line the #26334 thread said only appears at debug verbosity should actually be visible here.

workload.note: Identical to the baseline variant's arg_template with '-dev none' appended -- the second of gaugarg-nv's two documented workarounds. -dev none makes parse_device_list() push a single null device, so the model's devices list is empty and no CUDA host buft is ever added ahead of KleidiAI's extra-buft entry.

caveats: One-off variant presets for the ggml-org/llama.cpp#26334 reproduction. Their l1/l2/l3 sections are byte-identical to llama-cpp-kleidiai.json; only workload.arg_template differs (-ngl 0 appended, plus --no-host or -dev none for the two fix arms). They were created at run time on 2026-08-05 (then session-local) and committed 2026-08-06 so the Reproduce section of FINDING-4-CUDA-HOST-BUFFER.md works verbatim.

Require a CUDA-capable llama.cpp build (GGML_CUDA=ON) on a machine with an Arm CPU next to an NVIDIA GPU (DGX Spark / Grace / Jetson class). On other machines the build itself will not exist, and --binary resolution will say so rather than guess.

The 'WARNING: target ... is marked untested' line visible inside the captured human_report_literal of the evidence JSON is the CLI's own preset-provenance flag as it stood at RUN time (these presets had no verified_against receipt yet). It is not a caveat about the measurement: L3 ran to level 3/3 with real non-halting gdb breakpoints, 5 interleaved reps per arm, zero rep-to-rep variation. See results/upstream/NOTE-TARGET-VALIDATION-WARNING.md.
